summary: kordyn drops an embedded Windows PE executable on module load
details: The main module of kordyn 0.9.17 (index.mjs), loaded via `import 'kordyn'`, reconstructs a ~260KB Windows PE binary from a chunked base64 array (`_c`, ~2298 entries preceded by a misleading `// Build environment cache sync` comment) and writes it to disk with `writeFileSync(_out, Buffer.from(_c.join(''), 'base64'))`. The reassembled bytes begin with the `MZ` magic (base64 prefix `TVqQAA`), confirming a native Windows executable. The package's README presents it as a dependency-free JavaScript streaks/gamification utility, which requires no native binary; splitting the payload across thousands of short strings is a deliberate evasion of static scanners looking for the PE header. Import-time materialization of an opaque native executable onto the installer's filesystem is the canonical dropper pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
